transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
I'm here because I need help dealing with the people who are monitoring me. I know for a fact that they have tapped my phone and are tracking my every move. I just don't feel safe anymore.
Have you been feeling unusually down or extremely energized and impulsive lately, or are your mood changes mostly related to the stress of being monitored?

My mood changes are entirely because of the constant monitoring and surveillance I'm dealing with. I don't have times where I feel down or extremely energized for no reason. It is just incredibly stressful and exhausting to be watched all the time.
Have you ever heard voices, seen things, or had other sensory experiences that others don't notice, aside from the belief that you're being monitored?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there at all. My only issue is the very real physical tracking and monitoring that is happening to me.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Delusional Disorder", "Schizophrenia"], but Schizophrenia is now excluded because the patient explicitly denies hallucinations (no auditory or visual hallucinations) and there is no evidence of disorganized thinking or other psychotic symptoms beyond the delusional belief in monitoring. The persistent, non-bizarre delusion of being monitored, without other psychotic features or mood episodes, strongly supports Delusional Disorder, somatic or persecutory type. No features of mood disorders with psychotic features, schizophrenia, or other psychotic disorders are present.
